claim: Visitor arrival, imaginary tasks and humorous reactions are openly illustrative framing, not a recovered diary.
locator: Narrative framing, explicitly stated in S006.
limit: No invented historical dialogue, payments, individual biography or exact day schedule.

claim: QAR was Blackbeard's flagship; previously the French slave ship La Concorde, captured in 1717.
locator: Exploring the Vessel's Origins; Beginning of the End; Encountering Blackbeard.
limit: Never imply a pirate takeover freed everyone, nor specify unverified construction date.

claim: Recovered butchered cattle and pig bones indicate meat provisions, but may include pre-pirate provisioning.
locator: Bone identification and Mindin/West Africa provisioning paragraphs.
limit: Presence is not a dated menu, quantity, quality, or each pirate's diet.

claim: Georges Bardeau, La Concorde's second cook, was forcibly retained by pirates; continued work as cook is plausible but unproven.
locator: Bardeau paragraph and cited Ernaut deposition, 27 April 1718.
limit: Say force explicitly; no actor represented as exact likeness.

claim: Recovered tools attest carpentry, sailmaking, rigging, navigation and other practical skills.
locator: Tools overview; iron gouge flattened head and hammering.
limit: Illustrative action based on tool function, not a witnessed workday. Do not use uncertain silver needle as a sail needle.

claim: A lead sounding weight on a line measured water depth and helped identify bottom consistency.
limit: Only large securely identified weight; no invented numerical depth or assurance of safety.

claim: Recovered dividers are associated with chart navigation; a brass mortar and pestle with preparation of medicines.
locator: Dividers purpose paragraph; mortar and pestle function.
limit: Reconstructed use, not a named owner's tools or proof of effective treatment.

claim: A 1724 account describes Blackbeard holding vessels and demanding a medicine chest at Charleston.
locator: Blackbeard chapter: Teach detained ships and prisoners, demand for medicines, release after compliance.
limit: Attribute written account, omit disputed values and invented dialogue. Not evidence any one recovered mortar came from that chest.

claim: Johnson's account attributes bans on gambling for money and lights-out at eight to Roberts's crew, with drinkers outside afterward.
locator: Roberts articles III–IV; author's admission attempts to curb drinking were ineffective.
limit: Another captain, after QAR's career; written rule not proven perfect compliance; no exact universal bedtime.

claim: Sixteen tiny paper fragments recovered from a cannon chamber were identified as part of Edward Cooke's 1712 voyage narrative.
limit: Cannot identify who read it, when it was torn, why it entered chamber, or what all pirates read.

claim: The recovered tools and provisions support an interpretation of practical labor between raids, without supplying a complete timetable.
locator: Synthesis of object functions, contrasted with unknown individual routines.
limit: Explicit reconstructed sequence, not hours per task or all-crew uniform routine.

claim: The large silver needle has debated interpretations; softness and size complicate sail or medical use, and a sacking needle is one possibility.
limit: No definite identification or specific task depicted.
